title: U.S. House · New York's 8th Congressional District
area: Central and southern Brooklyn, including Brownsville, East New York, Canarsie, Coney Island, and parts of Crown Heights.

context.text: Incumbent Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic Leader, advanced unopposed after the Democratic primary was canceled (challengers Vance Bostic and Chi Osse withdrew or were disqualified). Lewis Mizrahi advanced unopposed after the Republican and Conservative Party primaries were canceled.
Mizrahi also filed to run in New York's 9th Congressional District but was disqualified from that district's Republican primary; he remains on the ballot only in the 8th District.

candidates.name: Hakeem Jeffries

summary.text: Hakeem Jeffries is the incumbent U.S. Representative for NY-8 and the House Democratic Leader, first elected to Congress in 2012 after serving in the New York State Assembly. As Democratic Leader since 2023, he leads House Democrats' floor strategy and messaging rather than serving on standing committees.

background.text: Born in Crown Heights, Brooklyn; earned a B.S. in political science from SUNY Binghamton, a master's in public policy from Georgetown University, and a J.D. from NYU Law School.
Practiced law at Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison and Godosky & Gentile, and served as in-house counsel for Viacom and CBS before entering elected office.
Represented the 57th District in the New York State Assembly from 2007 to 2013 before being elected to Congress in 2012.

Elected House Democratic Leader for the 119th Congress by House Democrats on November 19, 2024, running unopposed; first became Democratic Leader in 2023 as chairman of the House Democratic Caucus's successor leadership post.

As Democratic Leader during the 2025 federal government shutdown (October 1 - November 12, 2025), led House Democrats' opposition to the initial continuing resolution; the shutdown ended after the House passed an amended funding bill 222-209 on November 12, 2025.

priorities.text: His office lists affordable housing development, criminal justice system reform, prescription drug price reduction, and educational access and quality among his primary focus areas.
Describes his work as "fighting for everyday Americans" on health care costs, housing affordability, job creation, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.

record.text: Serves on no standing committees as House Democratic Leader for the 2023-2026 period, a customary practice for the top party leader in the chamber.

Introduced H.Res. 625, recognizing the 50th anniversary of the independence of the Republic of Cabo Verde, in the 119th Congress; most of his recently introduced measures in this Congress have been ceremonial resolutions rather than substantive legislation, consistent with his role setting the chamber's floor agenda as party leader rather than sponsoring bills.

candidates.researchNotes: As House Democratic Leader, Jeffries holds no committee assignments and has sponsored little substantive legislation in the current Congress (leadership duties like floor scheduling and caucus messaging are not individually documented with citable official records); floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Lewis Mizrahi

summary.text: Lewis Mizrahi is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee against incumbent Hakeem Jeffries in NY-8. He has not filed a principal campaign committee with the FEC, has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and has little public campaign material available.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, FEC committee filing, or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey could be found for Lewis Mizrahi. FEC records show no committee registered and no funds raised as of the research date. He also filed to run in NY-9 but was disqualified from that district's Republican primary.
